we have developed an approach to identify root causes for reported problems using the concepts of dynamic behavior modeling and dependency graph.

the use of dependency graphs and run-time behavior models of resources in an I/T environment can be used to design algorithms to quickly identify root causes of problems and thus reduce administrative costs.
the combination of dependency graphs and runtime behavior models can be effectively used to determine the root cause of problems in an I/T environment.

the development of a framework that uses dependency information to model the I/T environment and uses the behavior of the modeled resources to predict and detect problems.
the development of a methodology for rapid problem determination using dependency graphs and run-time behavior models of resources that comprise a complex I/T environment.

the following problem: given a set of resources that comprise a system, and the dynamic performance characteristics (i.e., behavior model) of these resources, how to quickly and accurately determine the root cause of a reported problem in the system.

our approach is able to provide a systematic method for root-cause analysis and automated problem remediations.

our research work has resulted in a new and novel approach for problem determination in e-business I/T environments, and that this approach has the potential for significantly improving problem determination and resolution time, and thereby reducing administrative costs.

the approach presented in this paper is a significant step in the direction of automated problem determination in an e-business environment.

the dependency information and runtime behavior characteristics of resources in the I/T environment are key to rapid problem diagnosis.
